New facility-phase research: operator field set from blank to Mayo Clinic (not Epic Systems) based on Mayo Clinics Rochester MN world headquarters directly matching this facilitys location; Epic Systems is headquartered in Verona WI and is Mayo Clinics electronic health records software vendor, not a co-located data center operator, so this facility is read as Mayo Clinics own infrastructure running Epic software.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Mayo Clinic originated from William Worrall Mayos medical practice established in Rochester, Minnesota in 1864, and per Wikipedia became a nonprofit group medical practice in 1919 following the 1889 opening of Saint Marys Hospital by the Sisters of Saint Francis in partnership with the Mayo physicians; the organization is headquartered in Rochester, Minnesota, with additional major campuses in Jacksonville, Florida and Phoenix/Scottsdale, Arizona, plus a London facility opened in 2020, employing more than 7,300 physicians and scientists and roughly 66,000 support staff, and has been ranked the number one overall hospital in the United States by US News and World Report for multiple consecutive years.

Separately, per Wikipedia, Epic Systems, a Verona, Wisconsin-headquartered electronic health records company founded in 1979, provides electronic record systems for all Mayo Clinic campuses, though this is a software vendor relationship rather than a shared data center operator relationship; Epic Systems own Wikipedia page did not mention operating any Rochester, Minnesota data center facility. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as Epic / Mayo Data Center in Rochester, Minnesota, was not individually named in any prior operator-level research; its operator field was blank in the source data and is set here to Mayo Clinic, whose Rochester, Minnesota world headquarters directly matches this facilitys location, rather than to Epic Systems, which is headquartered in Verona, Wisconsin and supplies Mayo Clinic only as a software vendor, reasoning that this facility most likely represents Mayo Clinics own data center infrastructure running Epic electronic health record software rather than a facility owned or operated by Epic Systems itself.
